review_notes: I read the whole file and its test file, AdicModulesTest/Topology/Algebra/PrincipalUnits.lean, to see how the lemmas are used. I also checked that Mathlib's `MonoidHom.mem_ker` is a simp lemma. I did not run Lean. The only simp-interface problem I found is the missing natural and integer cast reduction for `padicPow`. I considered making `mem_ker_unitsMap_quotient_iff` or `padicPow_add` simp. I rejected both: the first would compete with the simp lemma `MonoidHom.mem_ker`, and the second would expand sums of exponents.

findings.excerpt:
theorem padicPow_intCast (n : ℤ) (v : K) :
    I.padicPow p hpI (n : ℤ_[p]) v = v ^ n := by
findings.problem: The simp set covers only the exponents `0` and `1` (`padicPow_zero`, `padicPow_one`). The identity that reduces `padicPow` at an integer exponent to an ordinary power is not simp. The cast form `((n : ℤ) : ℤ_[p])` is also not simp-normal, because `Int.cast_natCast` rewrites `((n : ℕ) : ℤ) : ℤ_[p])` to `(n : ℤ_[p])`. So even with `padicPow_intCast` tagged simp, it would not fire on exponents such as `(p : ℤ_[p])`. There is no `ℕ`-cast version and no numeral version either. The test file works around this by hand. For `(p : ℤ_[p])` it instantiates the lemma at `(p : ℤ)` and calls `simpa only [Int.cast_natCast, zpow_natCast, ...]`. For the exponent `2` it calls `simpa only [Int.cast_ofNat, zpow_ofNat, ...]`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `padicPow_intCast` `@[simp]`. Add companion lemmas stated in the simp-normal cast forms. One is `padicPow_natCast (n : ℕ) (v : K) : I.padicPow p hpI (n : ℤ_[p]) v = v ^ n`, also `@[simp]`, with the proof going through `padicPow_intCast` and `Int.cast_natCast`. The other is the same for numerals, `OfNat`, with `n.AtLeastTwo` if needed. Keep the left sides as `padicPow (cast n) v` with the right side a plain monoid power, so there is no loop. These coexist with `padicPow_zero` and `padicPow_one`: for `0` and `1`, `Nat.cast_zero` and `Nat.cast_one` normalize the cast first.
findings.benefit: Computations such as `padicPow (p : ℤ_[p]) (oneAddX p)` or `padicPow 2 minusOnePrincipal` reduce directly to `v ^ n` by `simp`. The tests then no longer need to instantiate the lemma at an integer and juggle `Int.cast_natCast`/`Int.cast_ofNat`/`zpow_natCast` in `simpa only` calls. The `(p : ℤ_[p])` exponent is the natural exponent in applications (Frobenius-type power), and the Nat-cast normal form is the one simp produces.
